title: How Axon's voice line answers a question
subtitle: Deepgram hears, Axon's guarded chat agent answers, and ElevenLabs speaks each sentence as soon as it's written.
hook: Ears, brain and voice are separate, so the voice line reuses the chat's guard, retrieval and knowledge.

nodes.label: Visitor
nodes.detail: Someone on the site presses Start a voice call and talks. Their browser streams the microphone straight to Deepgram.
nodes.tradeoff: Echo cancellation in the browser keeps Axon's own voice from being heard as the visitor talking.

nodes.label: Token minting
nodes.detail: A Pages Function rate-limits the caller, then asks Deepgram for a 30-second token. The browser opens its speech connection with that, never with the API key.
nodes.tradeoff: The token only has to live long enough to open the connection, so the microphone is requested first.

nodes.label: Speech to text
nodes.detail: Nova-3 transcribes as the visitor speaks and uses endpointing to decide when they have finished, so Axon doesn't answer mid-sentence.
nodes.tradeoff: A longer silence threshold avoids cutting people off but adds a beat before every reply.

nodes.label: Guard
nodes.detail: The same code guard as the chat: off-topic and prompt-injection checks, size limits and per-visitor rate limits, before any model is called.
nodes.tradeoff: Refusing in code is instant and free, but only catches what the rules describe.

nodes.label: Axon chat agent
nodes.detail: The finished sentence goes to the same agent as the chat, asked for a short spoken reply: one to three sentences, no lists or links, with page actions as hidden tags.
nodes.tradeoff: One agent for chat and voice means one knowledge base to keep right, at the cost of a text step a speech-to-speech model would skip.

nodes.label: Knowledge cards
nodes.detail: A BM25 retriever picks the cards that answer the question, so spoken answers come from the same written facts as the chat's cited ones.
nodes.tradeoff: Curated cards keep answers accurate, but anything not written down, Axon can't say.

nodes.label: Axon's voice
nodes.detail: Each sentence is sent to ElevenLabs Flash as soon as it's complete and played while the next is fetched, in the same designed voice as the guided tour.
nodes.tradeoff: Sentence-sized requests start speaking sooner, but each one is a separate round trip.

nodes.label: Voice budget
nodes.detail: ElevenLabs bills by character, so speech has a per-visitor and a daily character allowance. When it runs out the call keeps going in the browser's own voice.
nodes.tradeoff: A hard cap protects the bill, at the price of a plainer voice on a busy day.

nodes.label: Page actions
nodes.detail: A tag at the end of a reply scrolls the page to a project, opens the contact form, or ends the call after the goodbye has played.
nodes.tradeoff: Tags in the text are simple and work with any model, but rely on the model following the format.

flow.text: The visitor asks a question out loud.
A 30-second token lets the browser reach Deepgram without the key.
Nova-3 transcribes live and marks when the visitor has finished.
The guard checks it, cards are retrieved, and a short spoken answer streams back.
Each finished sentence plays in Axon's ElevenLabs voice while the next is written.
A tag in the reply scrolls the page to what Axon is talking about.
If the visitor cuts in, playback stops and Axon listens again.

takeaways.text: Splitting ears, brain and voice lets the voice line reuse the chat's guard, retrieval and knowledge instead of a second prompt.
Speaking sentence by sentence starts the voice before the whole answer is written.
Speech is billed by character, so it has a daily budget and falls back to the browser's voice when that runs out.
